t.1.53.1: We have heard this other most wondrous thing concerning Āstīka, when he was thus being tempted with boons by King Pārikṣita.
t.1.53.2: Because the serpent, fallen from Indra's hand, remained standing in the sky itself, King Janamejaya then became absorbed in anxious thought.
t.1.53.3: Then, even as offerings were being poured according to the rite into the fiercely blazing fire, Takṣaka, tormented by fear, did not fall into the flames.
t.1.53.4: Śaunaka said: Why, O Sūta, did the array of mantras of those wise Brahmins not prevail then, so that Takṣaka did not fall into the fire?
t.1.53.5: To that foremost of serpents, who had slipped from Indra's hand and lay senseless, Āstīka uttered three times the words, "Stop! Stop!"
t.1.53.7: Then the king, strongly urged by the members of the assembly, spoke these words: "Very well, let it be so, just as Āstīka has spoken."
t.1.53.8: Let this rite be brought to an end, let the serpents be free from harm, let this Āstīka be gratified, and let that word of the Sūta prove true.
t.1.53.6: Then he stood suspended in the sky with an anguished heart, just as a man might stand caught between the wheels of an ox-cart.
t.1.53.9: Then, when the boon had been granted to Āstīka, a joyful cry of "halahalā" arose, born of delight, and in the same way it died down.
t.1.53.11: To the officiating priests together with the members of the assembly, and to those who had gathered there, he gave wealth by the hundreds and then by the thousands.
t.1.53.10: Such was that sacrifice of the king, the descendant of the Pāṇḍavas, the son of Parikṣit; and King Janamejaya, the Bhārata, was filled with delight.
t.1.53.12: The lord likewise gave wealth to Lohitākṣa, the sūta and master builder, who had foretold there, at the outset of the sacrificial session, that the sacrifice would be stopped.
t.1.53.14: The king, glad at heart, sent Āstīka back home, well honored, pleased, his purpose accomplished, that wise man.
t.1.53.15: And he spoke these words to him: "You must come again; you shall be a member of the assembly at my horse sacrifice, the great rite."
t.1.53.13: Remembering his word that a brāhmaṇa would be the cause, he gave him much wealth. Then he performed the concluding ablution of the sacrifice according to the rite laid down by injunction.
t.1.53.16: Saying "So be it," Āstīka, filled with joy, hastened away, having accomplished his own incomparable task and having pleased the king.
t.1.53.17: Having gone back, he, supremely delighted, approached his mother and that maternal uncle, and after clasping their feet in reverence, he reported to them all that had happened.
t.1.53.18: Hearing this, the serpents who were assembled there rejoiced, freed from their bewilderment; they became well-disposed toward Āstīka and said to him, "Choose the boon you desire."
t.1.53.19: Again and again they all said to him, "What pleasing thing may we do for you today, O wise one? We are pleased, and all of us have been set free; what wish of yours may we fulfil today, dear child?"
t.1.53.20: Those in the world, brahmins and other men as well, who with serene and gracious spirits recite this tale of dharma of mine in the evening and in the morning, let there be no fear whatsoever for them from you.
t.1.53.22: May the greatly renowned Āstīka, true to his word, born of Jaratkāru in Jaratkāru, protect me from the serpents.
t.1.53.23: Whoever remembers Asita, Ārtimant and Sunītha, whether by day or by night, shall have no fear of serpents.
t.1.53.21: And the pleased serpents in turn spoke to their nephew: “This is true; let it be as you wish. Acting thus, filled with affection and devoted to you, we shall accomplish whatever you desire in every way, O nephew.”
t.1.53.24: Having freed the serpents from the snake sacrifice, that best of the twice-born, righteous in spirit and blessed with sons and grandsons, went in due time to his destined end.
t.1.53.25: Thus I have duly recounted to you the Āstīka tale, by reciting which there is never any fear of serpents anywhere.
t.1.53.27: Śaunaka said: Beginning from the lineage of Bhṛgu, you have narrated to me this great tale in its entirety, dear Sauti; I am pleased with you for it.
t.1.53.26: O brahmin, having heard the most righteous tale of Āstīka, which increases merit, the glorious story of the seer Āstīka from its very beginning…
t.1.53.28: And I shall question you further, as is proper, O son of a sūta; and that tale which was composed by Vyāsa, recount it to me once more.
t.1.53.30: The wondrous tales that arose concerning those matters, we wish to hear from you exactly as they were, O Sauti, for you are indeed discerning.
t.1.53.29: At that snake sacrifice, so very hard to attain, O great poet, during the intervals between the rites duly performed by the great-souled members of the assembly…
t.1.53.31: In the intervals between the rites, the twice-born told stories grounded in the Vedas, but Vyāsa constantly narrated the great Bhārata tale.
t.1.53.33: He then duly recited it during the intervals of the rite; that holy tale I wish to hear, in due order, indeed.
t.1.53.32: Śaunaka said: The Mahābhārata, the tale that brings glory to the Pāṇḍavas, about which Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana was then asked by Janamejaya…
t.1.53.35: Come then, I shall tell you from the beginning the great and supreme narrative, the Mahābhārata, as conceived by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.
t.1.53.34: O best of the virtuous, tell the tale that arose from the ocean of the mind of the great seer of holy deeds, for I am not yet satisfied, O son of the Sūta.
t.1.53.36: Enjoy that, O brahmin of the highest understanding, as it is being told by me; here, in recounting it, a joy of heart arises in me as well.
